tweets.text:
Recently had a long conversation with another designer who’s been for 2x the amount of time we have.

We’ve seen the shift.
Hard-coded backend and frontend.
WordPress.
Webflow.
Framer.
Now AI enabled sites.

And honestly, for most early-stage or bootstrapped founders, templates and AI-generated sites are a perfectly valid place to start.

But the more interesting question we keep coming back to at This Is It Studio is fundamental:

What actually is a website?

The first website existed to explain how to use the internet.

Decades later, the core interaction hasn’t changed.
Scroll.
Click.
Hover.
On a flat screen.

The visuals have improved.
The transitions are smoother.
But the concept hasn’t quite.

As our interactions with the web shift through voice, agents, gestures, and intelligent layers, that definition starts to feel outdated.

Designers going into 2026 shouldn’t be competing on execution speed or optimisation.

Agents will handle most of that.

The real work is rethinking what communication design looks like when the interface and interactions itself are variables.
